rules.explanation: Relying solely on username and password authentication makes user accounts extremely vulnerable to credential stuffing and phishing attacks.
rules.do: Enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) across all administrative portals, cloud consoles, and user authentication systems.
rules.dont: Do not permit single-factor password authentication for privileged system accounts or administrative dashboards.

rules.rule_name: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and Least Privilege
rules.explanation: Assigning broad or wildcard permissions to users or services compromises access boundaries and violates security isolation.
rules.do: Implement fine-grained Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) or Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC), assigning permissions based strictly on functional job needs.
rules.dont: Do not grant wildcard (*) permissions or overly broad access rights to general user roles.

rules.rule_name: Industry-Standard Cryptographic Algorithms and Key Management
rules.explanation: Using deprecated encryption algorithms (e.g., MD5, SHA-1, DES) or hardcoding cryptographic keys weakens data confidentiality.
rules.do: Use modern cryptographic standards (e.g., AES-256 for symmetric encryption, RSA-2048+/ECDSA for asymmetric, SHA-256+ for hashing) and manage keys securely via dedicated key management services.
rules.dont: Do not implement custom cryptographic algorithms or use broken legacy hashing functions for sensitive data.

rules.rule_name: Token Expiration and Secure Token Revocation
rules.explanation: Issuing long-lived JWTs or API access tokens without expiration limits or revocation mechanisms increases exposure window if tokens are leaked.
rules.do: Configure short-lived access tokens paired with secure, revocable refresh tokens and implement token blacklist or revocation checks.
rules.dont: Do not issue permanent access tokens or JWTs that never expire without a secure renewal mechanism.
